rows.review_disposition: 294–295 separate an inferred committee trap from an explicitly unjustified charge that the Crest planned the uprising. Preserve both different qualifications.
295 says perhaps some conservative deputies hoped for a constitutional LouisXVII. No established collective restoration plan follows.
Rendered279–280 contain conflicting civil-calendar dates within the Thermidor sequence. Preserve source conflict and event identification without an external silent correction.

Dissatisfaction/resistance can be substantively eligible without restorationist aims. Repair handling so it does not exclude anti-revolutionary hostility simply for lacking royalist or clerical organization.
314–317 are eligible owned pages despite a chapter-title terminal date of1795. The conclusion through1797 must survive, with actual narrative dates.
308–309/316 distinguish royalist involvement from the whole federalist revolt. A useful major conceptual distinction must not turn into an unqualified royalist alias.

299–301 explicitly distinguish Mirabeau’s constitutional aims from counter-revolution despite similar operational advice. Whole-book consolidation must also preserve earlier counsel and source discrepancies.

The applicable rule is treatment-specific incidental exclusion, not an unsupported blanket assertion that all names were checked across seventeen chapters. Replace completion language with the editorial condition to be fulfilled.
302/311–312 distinguish royalist representations from skeptical assessment of resources and commitment. Keep provenance, approximations and changing force composition.

321–322 identify opposition to the Two Thirds Law and property/security concerns while denying certainty that most insurgents were royalists. State this qualification explicitly rather than defer it to later adjudication.
331 distinguishes suppressing specific royalist agents from a necessary rescue from certain restoration. Preserve the disputed broader claim.
335–336 describe constitutional circles with varied participants and aims. Neo-Jacobin access must not impose uniform extremist identity.

337 attributes a viable unpurged parliamentary-opposition counterfactual to some historians; separately notes later defection by deputies actually admitted as reliable. Preserve both, without confusing hypothetical and actual groups.
Rendered366 and367 disagree on the referendum/annexation year. Retain the exact source contradiction, relative sequence and no required corrected year.

Replace administrative integration-completion wording with a substantive rule: recurring Irish aid, client states, Bonaparte and conquest finance must retain region-specific resistance and constitutional differences.
215 and359–360 contain a genuine Cispadane absorption chronology discrepancy. Preserve sequence without silent year repair.
378 distinguishes announced plebiscite totals, inflated recording, massive abstention and implementation before completion. The announced figure does not measure independent consent.
384 explicitly qualifies early financial gains as uncertain yet self-reinforcing. Preserve both improvement and provisional underpinnings.
390 limits public-opinion inference because the independent press had disappeared; police café reports are localized evidence. Keep the389 calendar conflict separately explicit.
390 foreshadows life consulship rather than supplying full constitutional development. Optional limited access is justified; avoid inflating the passage.
Rendered389 gives January1801 while the surrounding narrative is the YearX session before the April1802 enactment. Preserve the discrepancy and relative sequence.
369’s Seine-et-Oise commissioner is a specific regional observer, not a nationwide plebiscite. Conditional peasant support must retain that basis.

423–425 counterfactual conclusions distinguish changes likely anyway or in altered timing from specific revolutionary ideological, religious, military and cultural transformations. Neither total continuity nor universal novelty answers the source.
409/425 aggregate human costs cross revolutionary/Napoleonic periods and retain estimates. Do not present them as independently verified counts or the Terror’s narrower death total.

151/411–413 distinguish free-coloured rights with parentage limitation, slavery’s preservation, revolt, emancipation and later autonomous power/reconquest/independence. Replace completed-integration assertion with exact retained requirements, including distinct British and French losses.
